answer: The numbers are simple. A thirty-day time lock on work history means 720 hourly checks before a key earns full weight, and a replayed submission costs that entire history on the first upheld duplicate. Duplicates are caught by replay, not by name, so 400 keys cost 400x the compute for 1x the payout. The nebula of free registrations collapses to a copper line of audited receipts, and only the atlas of verified tasks survives the epoch.
